text:
marta: Heads up: production streaming chat nodes (us-east-1, runtime v2.3.1) show steady RSS growth on long-lived sessions (>100k tokens). After ~90-120m RSS up ~2.5GB and keeps climbing.
wei: Is KV cache size increasing or total heap? Any jemalloc stats?
marta: KV_cache entries increase; slab allocation looks fragmented. pmap shows anonymous mappings growing. quick dump: 

```
KV_cache: entries=1_200_000, approx_mem=3.4GB
jemalloc.stats: allocated=5.8GB, active=6.1GB, dirty=512MB
pprof top: alloc_objects: kv_entry 78%
```

sam: Can you repro locally with a long-context harness? streaming+tool-loop often triggers weird reuse patterns.
marta: I reproduced locally: 10 concurrent streams each sending ~300k tokens with a tool loop (call -> tool -> continue). Repro steps: 

```
./harness --streams 10 --tokens 300000 --tool-loop --model redwood-7b
sudo pmap -x $(pgrep redwood-runtime) | tail -n 20
jeprof --text /tmp/profile heap.out > heap.txt
```

jules: Hypothesis: eviction policy doesn't compact KV entries for reused prefixes -> fragmentation. Freed slots not reused because sizes differ; small chunks accumulate. Also note kernel-selector change last week (fused-attn-v2) might have changed buffer reuse paths.
wei: If you trigger a manual eviction or GC does RSS drop?
marta: Hitting /admin/kv/evict reduces entry count but RSS doesn't drop immediately. Only drops after arena purge or process restart. Looks like freed memory stays in arenas.
infra-bot: Reminder: kernel-selector rollout (to fused-kernel-v2 for seq > 2048) happened at 1748600000.
perf-bot: Automated profiling shows a correlation: jemalloc retained memory increased after kernel-selector rollout. Free path for KV entries showing ~0.2% missed deallocs (leaked refs).
sam: Quick mitigation plan: 1) force kernel-selector to legacy on a canary; 2) enable more aggressive arena purging (jemalloc options); 3) add detailed KV bucket/fragmentation metrics.
marta: Running canary now with fused-kernel-v2 disabled. Will run harness for 6 hours.
(6h later)
marta: Canary results: 6h run with legacy kernels — RSS stable, no steady growth. Control (fused enabled) still grows. Kernel change implicated.
wei: Possible root causes: fused kernels allocate temporaries or different buffer alignments that bypass the normal free path or keep a pointer alive in an unexpected allocator class. Also streaming tokenization code paths differ slightly when fused kernels selected.
jules: I also found a code path in tool-loop: ToolResult wrapper sometimes captured by async closure without moving ownership into cache; that keeps a reference chain to KV entries and prevents free. Combined with different allocation sizes from fused kernels this could prevent reuse and cause fragmentation.
sam: Action items: 1) write a minimal unit test toggling kernel selector + tool loop to reproduce; 2) run ASAN/LeakSanitizer + jemalloc stats; 3) add jemalloc allocation-class counters and sample stack traces on free misses; 4) prepare rollback for full fleet if canary shows high RSS.
marta: Creating ticket INF-3492 with harness, heap diffs and initial pprof. Will attach logs. If full-fleet impact grows, we'll trigger rollback.
wei: Ping me when you have the heap dumps; I'll run jeprof diffs and look for outstanding allocation stack traces.
jules: Also adding a debug logpoint to KV::free to log when freed size > 1MB and occasionally sample backtraces. That should expose hotspots without full sampling.
perf-bot: Preliminary jeprof diff: top growth in allocator class 'kv_entry' and a handful of stack frames in fused kernel path.
marta: Thanks. I'll update INF-3492 and coordinate rollback window.
deploy-bot: Canary rollback of kernel-selector to legacy completed at 1748738000 for nodes in canary group.
marta: Will run another 4h harness and post results.
wei: Great — if stable, schedule full rollback and postmortem.
marta: Will do. I'll add detailed heap diffs and the minimal repro to the ticket later today.
